description: As a Space Scientist skilled in GIS and data analysis, I'm passionate about using AI for space mission safety. Join my team to build an intuitive AI dashboard that translates NASA's microgravity fire data into life-saving insights for Moon/Mars missions! Seeking teammates skilled in: • AI / ML & NLP • UI/UX & Front-End Dev • Data Science & Engineering • Aerospace Research
summary: Firewise is an interactive, AI-powered dashboard built by Team Hephaestus that turns NASA’s scattered microgravity combustion research into clear fire-safety insights for human space exploration. NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository holds decades of flame experiments, but results are hard to find, compare, and interpret. Firewise addresses all three parts of the challenge. It summarizes each investigation and its documented test conditions, lets users compare experiments side by side, and interprets the evidence, highlighting research gaps for lunar habitats through an assistant whose answers cite their NASA sources. To demonstrate the approach, we analyzed one real PSI dataset from the ACME experiments on the ISS (347 ignition tests): at reduced pressure (7–8 psia), ignition rose from about 27% to 76% when oxygen increased from roughly 21% to 40%, though samples are small. This matters because fire is one of the most dangerous hazards in a sealed spacecraft, and flames behave differently without gravity. Firewise helps mission planners choose safer cabin conditions, shows where tests are missing, and can inform fire safety on Earth.
details:
FIREWISE – Fire-safety Evidence for Space Exploration

FIREWISE is an interactive, AI-powered web platform that transforms NASA's microgravity combustion research into accessible, structured, and useful insights to support fire safety in future human space exploration missions.

The platform organizes 24 NASA combustion investigations and 1,386 individual experimental tests, providing a unified environment where users can explore scientific findings, compare experimental conditions, and examine their relevance to spacecraft, lunar habitats, and Martian environments.

FIREWISE consists of five main components:

  • Investigations Explorer: Allows users to browse and compare NASA combustion investigations, experimental conditions, and documented findings.
  • Scenario Explorer: Enables users to configure environmental conditions and find the closest matching experimental evidence available in the NASA research database.
  • Digital Twin: Provides an interactive 2D and 3D simulation of a configurable space habitat. Users can adjust oxygen concentration, pressure, temperature, and gravity, visualize different environmental configurations, and examine calculated atmospheric properties. It focuses on simulating habitat environmental conditions rather than predicting actual fire behavior.
  • Research Gaps: Analyzes limitations and missing experimental evidence by comparing the available NASA research with the environmental requirements of future space habitats. This component represents the team's analysis of the available research.
  • AI Copilot: Uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and a Large Language Model (LLM) to retrieve relevant scientific information and generate context-aware answers grounded in the available research sources.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

FIREWISE makes the available NASA combustion research easier to access, explore, and understand. It supports evidence-based research and helps researchers and space-safety teams investigate environmental conditions relevant to safer spacecraft and future lunar and Martian habitats. Ultimately, FIREWISE aims to contribute to safer living environments for astronauts during long-duration space missions.

Technologies and Tools:

The platform was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the web interface, with Node.js for the backend. APIs are used to connect platform components and access the required data and services. The project also integrates a configurable Digital Twin for interactive habitat simulation, alongside Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Large Language Models (LLMs) to power the AI Copilot.

Creativity and Innovation:

Rather than simply displaying research papers or datasets, FIREWISE connects scientific evidence with interactive environmental scenarios, a configurable habitat simulation, an AI-powered research assistant, and research gap analysis. Bringing these capabilities together creates an accessible way to explore how existing microgravity combustion research can inform future space habitat safety.

Factors Considered:

The team considered the reliability and traceability of scientific sources, differences between microgravity and partial-gravity environments, atmospheric conditions in future habitats, missing or undocumented experimental values, and the limitations of the available research. The platform also distinguishes between documented experimental information, user-defined inputs, and calculated values to avoid presenting assumptions as experimental facts.
